decisions.reason: Define-XML ADLBC.AVISIT enumerates visit labels but no period value; both reported outputs contain a nonblank period string. Trimming its storage padding does not make it a listed code or a missing character value.

Retained Define-XML ADLBC.A1LO._ALB through ._URATE (beginning at line 7825) explicitly says 'Set to missing', while ordinary parameter ItemDefs copy LB.LBSTNRLO. The reported differences are on the change-parameter records governed by that missing-value rule, so the variable-level copy comparison applies the wrong rule to those records.

Retained Define-XML ADLBC.A1HI._ALB through ._URATE (beginning at line 7519) explicitly says 'Set to missing', while ordinary parameter ItemDefs copy LB.LBSTNRHI. The reported differences are on the change-parameter records governed by that missing-value rule, so the variable-level copy comparison applies the wrong rule to those records.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1LO divides by A1HI, the opposite normal limit from the lower-limit ratio named by its label and SAP page 12. These are different denominators, not alternative wording of the same ratio.

Lines 239-253 of adlbc-documented-rules.yaml run the Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1LO rule AVAL/A1HI at 1 digit and differ as reported, and the SAP page-12 limit reading still differs. adlbc.r L187-L189 computes R2A1LO = AVAL / A1LO and nothing later in the program rounds or overwrites it, so the R2A1LO__UNROUNDED reading is supported as how the reference was computed, not as documentation.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1HI divides by A1LO, the opposite normal limit from the upper-limit ratio named by its label and SAP page 12. These are different denominators, not alternative wording of the same ratio.

Lines 261-275 of adlbc-documented-rules.yaml run the Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1HI rule AVAL/A1LO at 1 digit and differ as reported, and the SAP page-12 limit reading still differs. adlbc.r L187-L190 computes R2A1HI = AVAL / A1HI and nothing later in the program rounds or overwrites it, so the R2A1HI__UNROUNDED reading is supported as how the reference was computed, not as documentation.
Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1LO states AVAL/A1HI at baseline, while the variable label and SAP page 12 identify the lower-limit ratio. The baseline qualifier does not reconcile the opposite denominator.

Lines 283-297 of adlbc-documented-rules.yaml run the Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1LO rule AVAL/A1HI on the baseline-flagged record at 1 digit and differ as reported. adlbc.r L187-L191 divides BASE (from derive_var_base at L117-L121) by the current record's A1LO with no later rounding, which supports the BR2A1LO__UNROUNDED reading as the reference computation, and the finding says it departs from the Define comment.
Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1HI states AVAL/A1LO at baseline, while the variable label and SAP page 12 identify the upper-limit ratio. The baseline qualifier does not reconcile the opposite denominator.

Lines 305-319 of adlbc-documented-rules.yaml run the Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1HI rule AVAL/A1LO on the baseline-flagged record at 1 digit and differ as reported. adlbc.r L187-L192 divides BASE (from derive_var_base at L117-L121) by the current record's A1HI with no later rounding, which supports the BR2A1HI__UNROUNDED reading as the reference computation, and the finding says it departs from the Define comment.

Lines 327-349 of adlbc-documented-rules.yaml keep both signed subtractions of Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL with 3-digit rounding, so the reported differences follow the literal rule. adlbc.r L193-L195 takes abs() of both terms and later steps (L199-L241) neither round nor overwrite ALBTRVAL, so ALBTRVAL__ABSOLUTE is supported as the reference computation, labelled as departing from the Define formula.

Define-XML ADLBC.STUDYID names ADSL.STUDYID, and dataguide.pdf page-4 lists STUDYID among the core variables merged from ADSL. adlbc_v1.yaml line 469 (base-ord) reads LB.STUDYID and the STUDYID column (lines 100-102) has no ADSL_SBJ derivation, so the documented ADSL source has no counterpart.

Define-XML ADLBC.STUDYID and dataguide.pdf page-4 name ADSL as the source of STUDYID. adlbc_v1.yaml lines 671-672 (base-eot) take ONLY(LB.STUDYID) and the STUDYID column (lines 100-102) declares no ADSL_SBJ derivation, so the stated source differs.

Define-XML ADLBC.STUDYID and data-guide page 4 explicitly name ADSL.STUDYID; adlbc.yaml row rule under-ord reads the identifier from LB, directly or through ONLY. ADSL_SBJ supplies other subject variables but does not replace that row-rule source, and matching identifiers as lookup keys does not establish the documented ADSL provenance.

Define-XML ADLBC.USUBJID and dataguide.pdf page-4 name ADSL as the source of USUBJID. adlbc_v1.yaml line 673 (base-eot) copies LB.USUBJID, a group_by key of that row rule (lines 665-668), and no derivation reads ADSL_SBJ.USUBJID.

ADSL_SBJ supplies other subject variables but does not replace that row-rule source, and matching identifiers as lookup keys does not establish the documented ADSL provenance.

SAP page-11 names laboratory assessments among those assigned to visits by actual visit dates relative to randomization, as an exception to the general CRF-visit convention stated just before it. adlbc_v1.yaml lines 490-512 (base-ord) map LB.VISIT labels directly, and no rule in adlbc_v1.yaml or adlbc_v2.yaml derives AVISIT from a date or study-day window.

Define-XML ADLBC.ADY names LB.LBDY, whereas adlbc.yaml lines 991-1005 calculate study_day from _ADT_DATE and TRTSDT. The row rules derive _ADT_DATE from LB.LBDTC and never read LB.LBDY, so this is a different source/computation even if values agree.

adlbc.yaml base-ord and under-ord explicitly copy LB.VISIT, and base-eot and under-eot retain LB.VISIT through ONLY on the selected source-record group. These row-rule derivations implement the source named by Define-XML ADLBC.VISIT; the empty column-level derivation is not a source difference.

adlbc.yaml base-ord and under-ord explicitly copy LB.VISITNUM, and base-eot and under-eot retain LB.VISITNUM through ONLY on the selected source-record group. These row-rule derivations implement the source named by Define-XML ADLBC.VISITNUM; the empty column-level derivation is not a source difference.

Define-XML ADLBC.PARAM builds the PARAMN<100 parameter by concatenating LB.LBTEST with LB.LBSTRESU. adlbc_v1.yaml lines 541-563 (base-ord) map LB.LBTESTCD to a fixed label dictionary, and PARAM (adlbc_v2.yaml lines 105-114) returns that label on non-shift rows, so neither documented source is read.

adlbc.yaml row rules base-ord and base-eot read LB.LBSTNRLO directly or through ONLY, while under-ord and under-eot set A1LO missing. Those branches implement the ordinary-copy and change-parameter missingness stated in retained Define-XML ADLBC.A1LO value-level ItemDefs (including line 7825); a missing column-level derivation does not establish a source divergence.

adlbc.yaml row rules base-ord and base-eot read LB.LBSTNRHI directly or through ONLY, while under-ord and under-eot set A1HI missing. Those branches implement the ordinary-copy and change-parameter missingness stated in retained Define-XML ADLBC.A1HI value-level ItemDefs (including line 7519); a missing column-level derivation does not establish a source divergence.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1LO specifies AVAL/A1HI, whereas adlbc.yaml R2A1LO uses _AVAL_BASE/A1LO. For ordinary parameters _AVAL_BASE is the source value, but the denominator remains the opposite documented limit.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1HI specifies AVAL/A1LO, whereas adlbc.yaml R2A1HI uses _AVAL_BASE/A1HI. For ordinary parameters _AVAL_BASE is the source value, but the denominator remains the opposite documented limit.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1LO specifies AVAL/A1HI at baseline; adlbc.yaml BR2A1LO instead divides _BASE by the current row's A1LO. The _BASE helpers select the baseline numerator but do not restore the documented denominator or explicitly select the baseline-record limit.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1HI specifies AVAL/A1LO at baseline; adlbc.yaml BR2A1HI instead divides _BASE by the current row's A1HI. The _BASE helpers select the baseline numerator but do not restore the documented denominator or explicitly select the baseline-record limit.

Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL takes the maximum of LBSTRESN-(1.5*ULN) and (.5*LLN)-LBSTRESN. adlbc_v1.yaml lines 618-624 (base-ord) take the greatest of 1.5*A1HI-_AVAL_BASE and _AVAL_BASE-0.5*A1LO, where A1HI, A1LO and _AVAL_BASE are LB.LBSTNRHI, LB.LBSTNRLO and LB.LBSTRESN (lines 478-479, 587), so both differences are reversed.

Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL specifies max(result-1.5*ULN, 0.5*LLN-result). adlbc.yaml under-ord instead takes the maximum of 1.5*_B_A1HI-_AVAL_BASE and _AVAL_BASE-0.5*_B_A1LO, reversing both subtractions.

SAP page-17 and define-adam.xml ADLBC.ABLFL.ALB (line 7969; the other ordinary parameters through line 8139 match) define baseline as Visit 1 ('Y if VISITNUM=1, null otherwise'), but adlbc_v1.yaml lines 536-540 (base-ord) test only LB.LBBLFL = 'Y'. define-sdtm.xml LB.LBBLFL (line 3511) derives that flag from VISIT="SCREENING", a value absent from the SDTM VISIT codelist (line 8830, which lists SCREENING 1 and SCREENING 2), so the specification does not state the documented VISITNUM=1 condition.

Define-XML ADLBC.AENTMTFL distinguishes Visit 12 from a last assessment selected for discontinuation before Visit 12. adlbc.yaml AENTMTFL and its _IS_LAST_ELIGIBLE/_IS_EOT helpers flag the last eligible scheduled record and its derived row without testing that early-discontinuation condition.

SAP page-12 asks for a flag on the last on-treatment observation, prior to or at week 24, for each lab parameter, which is an order in time. adlbc_v1.yaml lines 607-616 (base-ord) pick that record by descending LBSEQ, which Define-XML ADLBC.LBSEQ documents only as the sequence number copied from LB.LBSEQ, with no date or visit ordering.

SAP page 12 calls for the last observed on-treatment value, whereas adlbc.yaml under-ord orders eligible records by descending LBSEQ without an assessment-date ordering. Retained SDTM LB.LBSEQ (define-sdtm.xml line 3392) defines a sequential record identifier, not a guarantee of observation chronology.

SAP page-34 footnote [1] defines the end value as the last observed value while on treatment, prior to or at Week 24. adlbc_v1.yaml lines 810-820 (base-eot) select that record by descending LBSEQ, which Define-XML ADLBC.LBSEQ documents only as the sequence number copied from LB.LBSEQ, with no date or visit ordering.

SAP page 34 calls for the last observed on-treatment value, whereas adlbc.yaml under-eot orders eligible records by descending LBSEQ without an assessment-date ordering. Retained SDTM LB.LBSEQ (define-sdtm.xml line 3392) defines a sequential record identifier, not a guarantee of observation chronology.

These row-rule derivations implement the source named by Define-XML ADLBC.LBNRIND; the empty column-level derivation is not a source difference.

SAP page-11 assigns laboratory assessments by actual visit date with nearest-target and earlier-tie rules, but its window table lists only ADAS-Cog/CIBIC+ and NPI-X and page-12 gives no laboratory windows, so the documented rule is incomplete. adlbc.r L141-L169 maps CRF visit labels and builds End of Treatment rows, which shows how the reference was computed but documents no laboratory window.

Retained define-adam.xml ADLBC.AVAL value-level ItemDefs (ADLBC.AVAL.ALB at line 9013 'LB.LBSTRESN'; ADLBC.AVAL._ALB at line 9175 with the change-from-previous formula and 'null if LBBLFL=Y') state the rule, so the documentation is not incomplete; the obstacle is only the section adapter. adlbc.r L94-L99 shows the reference computation and adds no documentation.

Retained define-adam.xml ADLBC.BASE.ALB (line 9355) states 'ADLBC.LBSTRESN when ADLBC.ABLFL=Y' and ADLBC.BASE._ALB (line 9517) 'Set to missing', so the rule is documented and only the section adapter omits it. adlbc.r L115-L121 shows how the reference was computed and is not documentation.

Retained define-adam.xml ADLBC.CHG.ALB (line 9985) states 'AVAL-BASE' and ADLBC.CHG._ALB (line 10147) 'Set to missing', so the rule is documented and only the section adapter omits it. adlbc.r L122-L123 shows the reference computation and adds no documentation.

Retained define-adam.xml ADLBC.ANL01FL.ALB (line 8293) flags the largest ALBTRVAL in Visits 4-12 with first-occurrence ties, and ADLBC.ANL01FL._ALB (line 8473) the largest absolute AVAL, so the metric and tie rule are documented and only the section adapter omits them. adlbc.r L209-L219 shows the reference computation, not documentation.

Retained define-adam.xml ADLBC.ANRIND.ALB (line 8653) states the 0.5*LBSTNRLO / 1.5*LBSTNRHI tests and ADLBC.ANRIND._ALB (line 8833) the change-parameter tests and null conditions, so the rule is documented and only the section adapter omits it. adlbc.r L196-L197 shows the reference computation, not documentation.

Retained define-adam.xml ADLBC.BNRIND.ALB (line 9661) states 'ADLBC.ANRIND when ADLBC.ABLFL=Y' and ADLBC.BNRIND._ALB (line 9841) 'Set to missing', so the rule is documented and only the section adapter omits it. adlbc.r L199-L202 shows the reference computation, not documentation.

Retained define-adam.xml ADLBC.ABLFL.ALB (line 7969) states 'Y if VISITNUM=1, null otherwise' and ADLBC.ABLFL._ALB (line 8149) 'Set to missing', so the rule is documented and only the section adapter omits it. adlbc.r L116 copies LBBLFL, which shows how the reference was computed and is not documentation.

Define-XML ADLBC.AENTMTFL conditions on discontinuation before Visit 12, and neither ADSL.DISCONFL (study discontinuation from DCREASCD) nor ADSL.VISNUMEN nor SAP pages 10, 12, 17 and 34 state how that condition is determined, and no value-level AENTMTFL ItemDef exists. adlbc.r L127-L180 flags ENDPOINT or Visit 12 rows and the maximum scheduled AVISITN, which shows the reference computation but documents no discontinuation test.

SAP page 11 includes laboratory assessments in the paragraph requiring selection of the assessment closest to the target day within a visit window. The AVISIT branches in base-ord/under-ord and the end-of-treatment row rules use visit labels and LBSEQ ranking, with no nearest-target selection counterpart.

SAP page 11 requires the assessment before the target day when two assessments are equidistant, in the same paragraph that includes laboratory assessments. No AVISIT branch or other rule in adlbc.yaml compares distances from a target day or applies this tie rule.
